sections.title: 2, 5 and 10
facts: $2$: last digit even. $5$: last digit $0$ or $5$. $10$: last digit $0$.
The remainder by $10$ is the last digit; by $5$ it is the last digit’s remainder by $5$.

sections.title: 3 and 9
facts: Add the digits. The number has the same remainder by $3$ (and by $9$) as its digit sum.
$10 = 9 + 1$ and $100 = 99 + 1$: that is why it works.

sections.title: 4 and 8
facts: $4$: look at the last two digits. $8$: look at the last three digits.
$100$ divides by $4$ and $1000$ divides by $8$, so the front part never matters.

sections.title: 6 and 11
facts: $11$: alternating sum $d_1 - d_2 + d_3$ (for a $3$-digit number) divides by $11$.
